Privacy Policy

Last updated 14 September 2026 · Effective 14 September 2026

The short version. We do not collect your personal data. There is no account to create, no analytics running, no advertising, and no third-party tracker anywhere in this game. Your saved progress lives in your own browser or on your own device, and it is never sent anywhere.

1. Who we are

“The Devil’s Dictionary” (the Service) is an independently produced word game, published on the web at devildictionary.com. Questions about this policy, or about anything below, go to support@devildictionary.com.

2. What this policy covers

This policy applies to the website, to any offline single-file edition of the game we distribute, and to any future mobile edition published under the same name. It does not cover websites, services or stores operated by other people, even when we link to them.

3. Information we do not collect

To be specific, we collect none of the following, and we have no system capable of collecting them:

  • Your name, email address, postal address or phone number.
  • Account credentials — because there are no accounts.
  • Precise or approximate location.
  • Contacts, photos, microphone input, health data, or anything else sensitive.
  • Payment card numbers, billing addresses, or Apple ID / Google credentials.
  • Advertising identifiers (such as IDFA) or any equivalent.
  • Analytics identifiers, session recordings, heatmaps or click tracking.
  • Device fingerprinting of any kind.

We keep no user database on any server. There is no profile attached to you, and therefore nothing about you that could be breached, sold, shared, or handed to a data broker.

4. Information stored on your device (never transmitted)

The game remembers your place so you can close it and come back later. That record is written locally and does not leave your machine:

  • On the web: your browser’s local storage holds one record, under the key devils-dictionary-save-v3. It contains only which entries you have already solved (the word names, nothing else), the entry you are currently playing, whether you have muted the sound, and whether you have seen the opening introduction.
  • On mobile: the same progress record is stored locally on the device, in exactly the same shape. Nothing is synced off it.

You can delete all of it at any time. On the web, use the RESET MY PROGRESS button in the footer of the game, or clear the site data for devildictionary.com in your browser settings. On mobile, reinstalling clears local data.

5. Purchases

There are none. The game sells nothing, so we never receive or store a card number, expiry date, billing address, or account password. There is no purchase ledger because there is nothing to record.

6. Hosting and incidental technical logs

The website is served by Vercel Inc. Like every host and content delivery network, Vercel necessarily handles basic request data in order to send you the page: your IP address, approximate region, user agent string, the URL requested, the timestamp, and the size of the response. We do not use those logs to identify you, profile you, or advertise to you, and we never combine them with anything else. How long those logs are kept and how they are secured is governed by Vercel’s own privacy practices.

7. Cookies and tracking technologies

We set no cookies. No analytics cookies, no advertising pixels, no third-party tags, no cross-site anything. The only storage in use is the local progress record described in section 4. Your browser’s “Do Not Track” preference is satisfied automatically, because there is nothing to track.

8. Children’s privacy

The Service is a general-audience reading puzzle. It is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. The game has no user-generated content, no chat, and no social features. If you believe a child has sent us personal information — for example by emailing us — write to support@devildictionary.com and we will delete it.

9. Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have rights of access, correction, deletion, portability, restriction and objection (for example under the GDPR in the EEA and UK), or rights to know, correct and delete (for example under the CCPA/CPRA in California). We do not sell or share personal information as those terms are defined in those laws.

For players, these rights are satisfied by a plain fact: we hold no personal data about you. The one exception is correspondence. If you email us, we hold that email thread so we can reply. Ask us to delete it and we will.

To make any request, write to support@devildictionary.com. We will answer within 30 days and will not charge you for it.

10. Security and retention

Because your progress lives on your own device rather than on our servers, keeping it private depends on keeping your device secure: use a device passcode and keep your operating system current. We keep no retention schedule of user data, because we retain no user data. Email correspondence is kept only as long as it takes to help you, unless a longer period is required by law.

11. Changes to this policy

If we ever change this policy we will update the date at the top. If a change is material, we will also say so on the main page of the game rather than quietly editing fine print. That last address remains the only place we ask you to trust.

12. Contact

Questions, complaints, or requests of any kind: support@devildictionary.com.
